July 30, 2026

U.S. launches new strike wave on Iran as Trump vows hard response

tags: war, politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy

U.S. Central Command said a two-hour strike wave hit dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets in Iran. The strikes followed Trump's vow of a hard U.S. response after Iran said it had fired missiles at U.S. sites in Jordan, and bombing was reported beginning at 8 p.m. Eastern time. Earlier the same day, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth met directly with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and envoys from both sides, a meeting critics said broke with the protocol that only the president or secretary of state hold such talks.

Alex Jones calls for Trump's impeachment and removal over Iran war

tags: politics, war
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Alex Jones, the former owner of Infowars and a repeated supporter of Donald Trump through the 2024 election, is now calling for the president's impeachment and removal from office. Jones said the president is out of control over the war in Iran, has not obtained congressional authorization for it, and is considering a national draft. He said the removal should come either through impeachment or the 25th Amendment.

Todd Blanche attorney general vote postponed for lack of support

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A Senate Judiciary Committee vote on Todd Blanche's nomination to be attorney general has been postponed indefinitely because he does not have the votes. Republican senators John Cornyn and Tom Tillis are the current holdouts; Cornyn cancelled a meeting with Blanche about a weaponization fund, saying Blanche had not done enough. Around ten Epstein survivors spent the day on Capitol Hill delivering binders of Epstein documents to Cornyn, Tillis and other Republican offices. With Mitch McConnell absent, the nomination may lack a path to confirmation.

Senate lacks votes to pass Trump's Save America Act

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Senate Majority Leader John Thune said the votes are not there to pass the Save America Act, telling reporters his math differs from the White House's. Trump has claimed he has the votes. Republicans also lack the votes to end the filibuster for the bill, and an attempt to move parts of it through reconciliation faces obstacles after the Senate parliamentarian previously ruled against it.

Trump administration seeks AI tools for pre-crime policing

tags: surveillance, legal, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

The Trump administration is seeking an artificial intelligence system for what it calls pre-crime policing, using government data on private citizens to predict crimes before they occur. The office pursuing the tools is the FBI's Terrorist Screening Center, which maintains the terrorist watch list. The categories of threats it examines have expanded to include anti-Christianity, anti-capitalism and anti-Americanism, extremism on migration, race and gender, and hostility toward those holding traditional views on family, religion and morality. Civil liberties critics warn the breadth could lead to individuals being targeted and their rights stripped.

DOJ sues Utah lieutenant governor over demand for full voter file

tags: elections, privacy, legal
sources: @carolinegleich

The Justice Department is demanding Utah's entire unredacted voter file, including birthdates, partial Social Security numbers and driver licence numbers for more than two million residents. Republican Lieutenant Governor Deidre Henderson refused, and the DOJ sued her and sent a letter warning she could face criminal penalties for following Utah law. A May state audit of 2,069,640 records found 99.72 percent were verifiable citizens, with 27 alleged and 25 probable noncitizens. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has threatened state election officials with possible prison time, and the DOJ has asked the Supreme Court to let Trump's executive order on mail voting take effect before the midterms; every court to rule so far has sided with the states.

Musk revives America PAC to spend heavily on Republican midterm turnout

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Elon Musk plans to spend tens of millions, and possibly hundreds of millions, of dollars in the midterm elections to help Republicans win up and down the ballot. Reporting from Axios says he is reviving America PAC, which spent over $260 million in 2024, with a focus on digital ads, door knocking and direct mail. Musk and the PAC have already been referred for possible criminal prosecution in Wisconsin over alleged election interference in the 2025 state Supreme Court race. The spending follows his falling out with Trump.

BLM moves to reopen 336,000 acres around Chaco Canyon to drilling and mining

tags: environment, government
sources: @carolinegleich

The Bureau of Land Management's preferred option would revoke the entire 10-mile protective buffer established around Chaco Canyon in 2023, reopening 336,000 acres to drilling, mining and uranium claims. The buffer contains more than 7,500 known historic sites and some of the darkest night skies remaining in the country, and Pueblo and Diné families live on and use the landscape. The agency's own assessment says under 1 percent of the land has development potential. The public comment period ran only 14 days and closed at midnight on July 29.

BLM approves first commercial AI data center on public land without new review

tags: tech, environment, government
sources: @carolinegleich

The Bureau of Land Management approved the Townsite Data Center on 88.5 acres of federal land in Eldorado Valley, Nevada, inside the limits of Boulder City, a community of fewer than 15,000 people. The facility would draw up to 167 megawatts, more than Boulder City itself consumes, and place two warehouse-scale buildings, a substation, battery storage, backup generators and a new road in desert tortoise habitat. The land had been designated for a solar farm, and BLM's Las Vegas field office manager approved the change in June without a new environmental assessment or public comment, calling it substantially the same because it sits in the same analysis area. Boulder City and two environmental organisations have filed appeals; the Sierra Club's Toiyabe Chapter said the approach could become a blueprint for data centers across public lands in the West. The decision follows a July 2025 executive order directing federal land and resources to be used for data center development.

Russian overnight barrage kills civilians in Ukraine as shelter gaps emerge in Kyiv

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Ukraine said Russian overnight strikes killed several people, including children, with more than 70 missiles and around 280 drones launched and Kyiv and Lviv the main focus. Dozens were injured across the country and Poland scrambled jets after a Russian missile crossed into its airspace. A record 56,000 people sheltered in Kyiv's metro in a single night, and officials say shelter shortages leave residents with few options. Russia said its strikes hit Ukrainian factories and three cargo ships, a claim Reuters could not verify.

Trump and Netanyahu weigh three options on Iran's nuclear program

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

A senior Israeli official said Trump and Netanyahu discussed three paths on Iran's nuclear program: a negotiated deal, a blockade combined with economic pressure, or a massive military strike.

U.S. sanctions eight tankers and ten entities over Iran

tags: politics, markets
sources: @oafnation_actual

The United States announced a new Iran-related sanctions action targeting eight tankers. Ten entities were also sanctioned, six of them based in China.

Fauci invokes Fifth Amendment before Senate committee

tags: politics, legal, health
sources: @aaronparnas, @ericmoutsos

Dr. Anthony Fauci repeatedly invoked the Fifth Amendment under oath before Rand Paul's Senate committee, saying he was acting on the advice of his attorneys. Republican senators including Josh Hawley said no honest person pleads the Fifth and suggested Fauci has something to hide, while a Newsmax contributor attacked him in cruder terms. Trump himself invoked the Fifth nearly 450 times during the New York attorney general's civil probe of his business practices. Asked about Fauci's pardon from President Biden, Trump questioned whether Biden personally signed it and suggested an auto-pen was used, saying he respected the pardon power but doubted the paperwork.

U.N. warns West Bank settler violence is worsening

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The United Nations warned that settler violence in the West Bank is worsening. U.N. figures cited by Reuters record 18 people killed in incidents linked to settler attacks so far in 2026, compared with 17 in all of 2025.

Democratic support for Israel continues to erode

tags: politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Israel is becoming an increasingly divisive issue within the Democratic Party. A Quinnipiac University poll from June 2026 found 66 percent of Democrats say the United States is too supportive of Israel, up from 20 percent in 2017.

Indiana data center construction cut power to tornado sirens before storms

tags: tech, climate
sources: @aaronparnas

A data center under construction in Linton County, Indiana cut power to the line feeding the county's tornado warning sirens ahead of severe storms, according to Linton News. The sirens were out of service for a period while the storms approached, though residents could still receive warnings by phone or online. Residents are angry both that the sirens had no backup generator and that the construction was able to sever their power supply.

McConnell's office stonewalls questions over month-long absence and signature

tags: politics, government
sources: @aaronparnas

Mitch McConnell's staff continue to decline questions about why no video of the senator has appeared in over a month. A letter dated July 28 on federal disaster relief funds for Kentucky carries a signature that differs from scans of wet signatures on his two prior letters in the past year, suggesting an auto-pen or digital generation was used — a practice common among legislators. Asked by a Capitol Hill reporter whether McConnell would release a video, his staff did not answer. McConnell has been discharged from hospital care and is in a rehabilitation facility.

Schools in three states deploy pepper-spraying drones against active shooters

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Nine schools across Colorado, Florida and Georgia are installing drones designed to confront active shooters. Footage obtained by the Washington Post shows a live reenactment in which the drones smash through windows and reach and pepper-spray a shooter within 15 seconds. Critics question both the effectiveness of the approach and the absence of legislative action on gun violence, and object to companies profiting from prevention measures.

Black Sea export disruptions push wheat prices higher

tags: markets
sources: @oafnation_actual

Chicago wheat prices edged higher as disruptions to Black Sea exports raised supply concerns. Russian grain terminals have restricted deliveries amid shipping risks.

State Department mislabels every African country on map at global AIDS conference

tags: government, health
sources: @aaronparnas

The State Department presented a map of Africa at a global AIDS conference in Brazil that mislabeled every country on the continent, according to Reuters Africa. Nigeria appeared landlocked in the Sahara, Mozambique was placed on the Horn of Africa, and Ivory Coast, Uganda, Malawi and Cameroon were also misplaced. The map spread widely online, with critics suggesting it was generated with AI.

White House account uses troops to promote nicotine pouches

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

The official White House account posted content citing consumption figures for U.S. troops — more than 6 million meals, an estimated 950,000 gallons of coffee, 2 million energy drinks and a large quantity of nicotine — in a post promoting Zyn. The post remains on the account.
